name: The Weeknd
label: XO/Republic
lede: He posted three songs under a username with no face, folded shirts at American Apparel, and ended up with a song that held a Hot 100 top-ten spot for a full year.

eras.title: Kin Kane in Parkdale
eras.text: Abel Tesfaye drops out at 17, moves into a Parkdale apartment with friends and folds shirts at American Apparel. He posts songs with no name, face or interviews attached, and by the end of 2010 Toronto wants to know who it is.

years.h: Nobody's name is on the first YouTube uploads
years.p: Abel Tesfaye was 19, a dropout who had sold cannabis and worked the floor at an American Apparel. The name came from a move: he went to Parkdale on a weekend and dropped the last 'e' to dodge a trademark.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Tesfaye left school at 17, lived on welfare checks in Parkdale with his friend [[La Mar Taylor|280b5ad7-c54d-4527-b746-d91a4672d157]] (now his creative director), and went through homelessness and jail before the music took off. Earlier aliases included Kin Kane, from the hip-hop duo Bulleez n Nerdz, and he had been part of a production team called the Noise.

The name comes from the move: he went to Parkdale on a weekend and dropped the final 'e' from 'weekend' to avoid clashing with a Canadian pop rock band called the Weekend.

years.h: Drake writes up three uploads from a username, xoxxxoooxo
years.p: 'What You Need', 'Loft Music' and 'The Morning' went up with no name attached. [[Drake|9fff2f8a-21e6-47de-a2b8-7f449929d43f]] wrote about them on his blog, and the first famous fan was in.
years.xp:
The three uploads picked up press from Pitchfork and the New York Times with no face and no name behind them. The Weeknd didn't do interviews yet.

Producer [[Jeremy Rose|33874ca1-1dba-427c-9c0f-93b38117e3a7]], who met Tesfaye at a party in 2010, co-produced songs from this period. [[Illangelo|faf9c4c1-fa6c-45a7-bd51-e91d8eed5577]] and [[Doc McKinney|f15651b5-67ab-43f5-8bb6-5a1138759e9e]] became his main producers in early 2011.

eras.title: Three free records in one year
eras.text: Tesfaye gives away three mixtapes in twelve months and plays his first live show with Drake in the room. Nobody has quite worked out whether the Weeknd is a person or a group.

years.h: Drake posts 'Wicked Games' two weeks ahead of the mixtape
years.p: He put it on his site on March 7, and the anonymous singer suddenly had an audience. Some fans took the Weeknd for a group.
years.xp:
The secrecy fed the curiosity: for a while it wasn't clear whether the Weeknd was one person or a collective.

The song is on House of Balloons, which came out two weeks later.

years.src: Wikipedia: House of Balloons · Wikipedia: The Weeknd
years.h: House of Balloons goes up free and makes the Polaris shortlist
years.p: Illangelo and Doc McKinney produced most of it, with Jeremy Rose and Cirkut on other tracks.
years.xp:
Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and called the production 'incredibly lush, downcast'. Metacritic averaged 87 across 16 reviews.

Exclaim! credited it with helping transform R&B, and the Fader's 2016 retrospective said it gave pop a new framework.

years.h: Drake is in the crowd for the Weeknd's first live show
years.p: At the Mod Club in Toronto, with Drake watching. The Weeknd then played Drake's OVO Fest on July 31, and 'High For This' turned up in an HBO Entourage promo the same month.
years.xp: The Mod Club was his first live performance, and the press that followed was mostly about who was standing in the room.

years.h: Two more free mixtapes before the year is out
years.p: Thursday came out August 18 and Echoes of Silence on December 21. Echoes was long-listed for the 2012 Polaris Prize.

eras.title: The major-label handshake
eras.text: Republic Records signs him in September 2012 and XO becomes a subsidiary. The mixtapes get repackaged as Trilogy, and the first studio album, Kiss Land, gets a cooler reception.

years.cap: Tesfaye at Music Hall of Williamsburg, Brooklyn, April 25, 2012
years.h: Republic Records signs him and XO becomes a label
years.p: XO, which he co-founded with Sal Slaiby and Cash Esmailian, becomes a Republic subsidiary. His first tour follows, including opening dates for Florence and the Machine.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trilogy (The Weeknd album) · Wikipedia: The Weeknd
years.h: Trilogy puts a price on the three mixtapes
years.p: They were remastered, with three new songs: 'Twenty Eight', 'Valerie' and 'Till Dawn (Here Comes the Sun)'. It debuted at No. 4 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp:
Selling the mixtapes meant clearing samples, including Beach House and Siouxsie and the Banshees. An Aaliyah sample was left out of the commercial release.

Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and called it 'some of the best music of the young decade'. Wikipedia notes some critics found the runtime indulgent.

years.cap: Tesfaye at Massey Hall, Toronto, October 17, 2013
years.src: Wikipedia: Kiss Land · Wikipedia: The Weeknd
years.h: Kiss Land plays like a horror movie shot on tour
years.p: Tesfaye cited John Carpenter, David Cronenberg and Ridley Scott. It debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200, and Pitchfork gave it 6.2.
years.xp:
Metacritic's score is 65 from 31 reviews. Reviewers liked the atmosphere and his falsetto, but some heard a re-run of the mixtape sound.

He toured it in theaters that fall, then opened for Drake in Europe and Justin Timberlake in North America.

eras.title: Fifty Shades, then the radio
eras.text: A movie single earns an Oscar nomination, then two No. 1s arrive in one summer. The mixtape singer becomes a pop star without changing his voice.

years.h: 'Earned It' brings an Oscar nomination
years.p: The Fifty Shades of Grey song peaked at No. 3 on the Hot 100 and earned his only Academy Award nomination, for Best Original Song. It also won a Grammy for Best R&B Performance.

years.h: 'The Hills' and 'Can't Feel My Face' both hit No. 1
years.p: 'The Hills' (May 27) and 'Can't Feel My Face' (June 8) both reached the top of the Hot 100. He also held all three top spots on Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs at once, a first.
years.xp:
'The Hills' was later certified diamond by the RIAA, his first diamond-certified song. Apple Music introduced him alongside Drake as a face of the service.

Both songs are on Beauty Behind the Madness, which followed on August 28.

years.h: Beauty Behind the Madness opens at No. 1, then keeps streaming
years.p: 412,000 units in its first week, and the most-streamed album of 2015 with over 60 million streams. It won Best Urban Contemporary Album at the Grammys.
years.xp:
It reached No. 1 in Canada, Australia, Norway and the UK and was nominated for Album of the Year.

Kanye West produced 'Tell Your Friends' on it, and he headlined Lollapalooza and Bumbershoot for it.

eras.title: A song that won't leave
eras.text: He gets Daft Punk on a No. 1 single, Kendrick Lamar on a Black Panther song and a six-song record at the top of the Billboard 200. Then comes 'Blinding Lights', which stays on the chart for years.

years.h: Daft Punk and the Weeknd reach No. 1 with 'Starboy'
years.p: Wikipedia lists it as his third No. 1, with Daft Punk credited on the single.

years.h: Starboy makes it two No. 1 albums in a row
years.p: 348,000 units in its first week, and another Grammy for Best Urban Contemporary Album. A short film, M A N I A, came with it.
years.xp:
He took it on the Legend of the Fall Tour through 2017.

'I Feel It Coming' peaked at No. 4 on the Hot 100.

years.h: Kendrick Lamar joins him on 'Pray for Me' for Black Panther
years.p: The song peaked at No. 7 on the Hot 100.

years.h: My Dear Melancholy, is six songs long and still tops the chart
years.p: 169,000 units made it the shortest album by track count to top the Billboard 200 in eight years. 'Call Out My Name' reached No. 4.
years.xp: He headlined Coachella for the first time on April 13, two weeks after the EP came out.

years.h: 'Blinding Lights' spends a full year in the Hot 100 top ten
years.p: It peaked at No. 1, and nobody had held a top-ten spot for a full year before. By November 2021 Billboard ranked it the best-performing song in the chart's history.
years.xp:
'Heartless' came out two days earlier and also reached No. 1. 'Blinding Lights' spent 90 weeks on the Hot 100, the longest run by a solo artist, and was the most-streamed song on Spotify by January 2023.

A Mercedes-Benz commercial teased it on November 24, 2019.

eras.title: The red suit
eras.text: After Hours gives him a character: a red blazer, a bloody nose and a Las Vegas hangover. The Grammys skip it, he says so in public, and then he plays the Super Bowl with his own money.

years.src: Wikipedia: After Hours (The Weeknd album) · Wikipedia: The Weeknd
years.h: After Hours arrives with a character and a bloody face
years.p: It topped the Billboard 200 and the Hot 100 in the same first week, and became the most-streamed R&B album of all time, passing his own Starboy.
years.xp:
The red-suited character was inspired by Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas and Joker. Producers included [[Max Martin|6622a50e-5206-44d0-9ad5-96047a726dcf]], [[Metro Boomin|59db3d82-86ea-451f-881f-dffc8ec387c9]], [[Illangelo|faf9c4c1-fa6c-45a7-bd51-e91d8eed5577]] and [[Oneohtrix Point Never|9cea062d-d476-447f-98b4-e67e14bfd1e4]].

He said the title refers to thoughts and emotions late at night, between 3 a.m. and 5 a.m.

years.big: "I have three GRAMMYs, which mean nothing to me now."
q: I have three GRAMMYs, which mean nothing to me now.
years.h: The Grammys skip After Hours entirely
years.p: The 63rd Grammys nominated neither the album nor 'Blinding Lights'. He called the awards 'corrupt' and pulled his performance.
years.xp:
He told Billboard the line above. The Recording Academy subsequently eliminated its private nominating committees.

He also said his label would stop submitting his work.

years.h: He pays about $7 million of his own money for Super Bowl LV
years.p: First Canadian solo artist to headline the halftime show. It drew three Emmy nominations.
years.xp:
The Highlights, his second greatest hits album, came out two days earlier and debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200.

Streams of After Hours and seven other performed songs jumped after the show.

years.src: Wikipedia: House of Balloons · Wikipedia: The Weeknd
years.h: The 2011 mixtapes come back with their original samples
years.p: For the tenth anniversary he re-released House of Balloons (March), Thursday (August) and Echoes of Silence (December) in their original form.

years.h: 'Take My Breath' rides NBC's Tokyo Olympics coverage
years.p: It was released with NBC Sports around the Games and peaked at No. 6 on the Hot 100.

eras.title: Purgatory radio
eras.text: He says the After Hours are over and the dawn is coming. Dawn FM turns the album into a fake radio station for the dead, with Jim Carrey as host.

years.src: Metacritic: Dawn FM · Wikipedia: Dawn FM
years.h: Dawn FM is a radio station in purgatory, and Pitchfork's No. 11
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.0, calling it his most ambitious project in sound and scope. It debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 and No. 1 in the UK, Canada and Australia.
years.xp:
He described it as a purgatory radio station: 'Picture the album being like the listener is dead.' It was recorded in Los Angeles and Stockholm in 2020 and 2021.

Metacritic scored it 88 from 24 reviews. The Guardian, Rolling Stone and NME gave it five stars; the Guardian ranked it No. 3 of 2022, Billboard No. 8 and Pitchfork No. 11.

Jim Carrey is the radio host, with voice parts from Quincy Jones and Josh Safdie. Producers include Oneohtrix Point Never, Max Martin, Calvin Harris and Swedish House Mafia; Tyler, the Creator and Lil Wayne guest.

years.h: Coachella again, this time with Swedish House Mafia
years.p: The trio who worked on Dawn FM and on 'Moth to a Flame' joined him for his second headline set.

years.cap: Tesfaye at Universal Studios Hollywood, October 19, 2022
years.h: After Hours til Dawn starts, and becomes the biggest male-soloist tour
years.p: The stadium run began in July 2022. It became the highest-grossing tour by a male soloist.

eras.title: Hurry up, tomorrow
eras.text: He floats retiring the name, makes an HBO series that gets cancelled and opens a new album at No. 1 anyway. The Weeknd keeps the name.

years.h: He floats retiring the Weeknd name
years.p: He said the next album could be a final hurrah under the name, and that he might go by his birth name or a new pseudonym.

years.h: The Idol reaches HBO and is cancelled after one season
years.p: He co-created it with Sam Levinson and starred with Lily-Rose Depp. HBO cancelled it on August 28 after one season, and the reviews were widely negative.

years.h: Hurry Up Tomorrow gives him a fifth No. 1 album
years.p: 490,500 units in its first week, his biggest opening by overall units. It includes 'Timeless' with Playboi Carti.
years.xp:
359,000 of those were pure sales, the most for a male artist since 2020.

'São Paulo' with Anitta followed in October 2024.

years.h: The film version grosses about half its $15 million budget
years.p: Trey Edward Shults directed it, with Jenna Ortega alongside him, and it made about $7.6 million. Critics mostly panned it.

years.h: Six straight sold-out nights at the Stade de France
years.p: Six consecutive shows in Paris in July 2026.
